faq.q: What is the origin of Khalida?
faq.a: Khalida is associated with Arabic. Khalida is Arabic خَالِدَة (Khālida) 'eternal, immortal' (feminine), from the root خ ل د (kh-l-d). The source gloss 'Eternal' is consistent. Same name as khaleda and khalidah.
Yes — the underlying form خالدة is Arabic.
Khalida can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: In Urdu, Khalida is rendered خالدہ and carries the sense خالدہ، ابدی (مؤنث).

faq.q: What does Khalida mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Khalida is rendered خالده and carries the sense خالده، جاویدان (مؤنث).
A romanized syllable approximation is kha-li-da. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Khalida?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Khalida, khalida. Script forms are خالدة, خالده, خالدہ, ख़ालिदा.

faq.q: Is Khalida a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
